preamble: Diphthongization of long [uː] to [au]. In the New High German diphthongization, Middle High German û became au [aʊ] (hûs > Haus), alongside î > ei [aɪ] and iu > eu [ɔʏ]; in many dialects the new au fell together with the old Middle High German diphthong ou, which was lowered to au. The English Great Vowel Shift is not filed here, because it went through dated diphthong stages: Middle English /uː/ of out was /ou/ (or /əu/) about 1500 and /ɔu/ about 1600 before it reached /aʊ/.

examples.note: New High German diphthongization of MHG ī, ū, iu to ei, au, eu (snîden > schneiden, liute > Leute). It started in Upper Bavarian in the 12th century and spread north and west. Alemannic (except Swabian) and Ripuarian keep [uː].

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Early New High German: Phonology. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_New_High_German
